A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All pages, including Appendices A and B, are readable, and the methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original simulations with randomly generated and clustered preferences, including algorithm comparisons in Table 1 and Figures 1–2.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original simulations and adds original algorithm evaluations using Sushi preference data in Section 5.4 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The scoring function, NSW objective, Fair-ETC, Fair-ε-Greedy and winner-identification procedures remain unchanged. The shared-feedback operation emphasized in v2 Section 4.2 already appears in v1 Appendix B; added pseudocode end markers clarify existing control flow.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic random and clustered preferences. v2 retains these and adds evaluations derived from the Sushi dataset of 5,000 individuals ranking ten items, extending coverage to recorded human preferences.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Utilitarian-ETC, Utilitarian-ε-Greedy and Uniform-Over-Users, including in the new Sushi experiment. Table 1 retains its best-per-metric Utilitarian column. Newly cited bandit methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added Sushi experiment introduces Spearman-distance clustering into D=5 or D=10 groups, cluster-level pairwise probabilities, projection of near-tie probabilities to 0.4 or 0.6, and 500,000-round evaluations. Existing synthetic protocols, metrics and hyperparameter values remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The majority/minority robustness experiment with clustering fractions 0.5 and 0.7 and its Figure 2 results are unchanged. The Sushi addition provides benchmark comparisons without a new dedicated ablation, stress test or error analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and 95% confidence regions over 30 independent runs. v2 retains this reporting practice and introduces no changed run count, seed disclosure or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds regret and four welfare/inequality outcomes for both Sushi configurations. Both fair methods have lower regret than the baselines; at D=10, Uniform-Over-Users achieves better minimum welfare and Gini scores. Existing Table 1 values and Figures 1–2 are unchanged, so these are additional findings under new conditions.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, scoring and regret definitions, Theorems 4.1–4.3, Lemmas A.1–A.2 and Appendix A proofs retain their mathematical content. Expanded DKWT explanations and retypeset equations do not introduce new formal results or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same fairness formulation, regret lower bound, two algorithms, matching horizon dependence and empirical fairness claims. The Sushi experiment adds supporting evidence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly explains ETC's lower computational cost but inability to correct poor estimates after commitment, versus ε-greedy's continued recovery and computation. v2 also justifies hyperparameter scaling and interprets the Sushi uniform baseline's D=10 fairness advantage as a tradeoff against higher regret.

D1.justification: Section 5.4 documents the Sushi construction: distance (1−Spearman correlation)/2, average-linkage agglomerative clustering, within-cluster ranking fractions and probability projection. These are reproducibility details for the added experiment. The existing Frank-Wolfe solver and numerical tuning parameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related Work adds Barman et al. (2023) and Sawarni et al. (2023) to discuss fairness across time. Additional citations support parameter tuning and Sushi preprocessing. These are limited expansions; the central positioning relative to earlier fairness and bandit research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section sequence are retained. v2 adds localized explanations and Section 5.4, removes the generic Impact Statement, and changes author and bibliography formatting. Some equation references become malformed, such as Equation equation 2.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with different typography, wider algorithm displays and substantially relocated figures and tables. A new ten-panel Figure 3 presents Sushi results. Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–2 retain their content while their placement and presentation change.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper with a documented Sushi evaluation beyond synthetic simulations and clearer explanations of algorithm operation and tradeoffs. The gain is limited because the new preferences are clustered and artificially margin-adjusted, while the core theory remains unchanged. Minor presentation regressions, including malformed equation references, temper the improvement.
